steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Welcome back, Echo!
When Echo arrives, Sally warmly greets her at the door with a hug, just like how they used to when they were in the orphanage. After that failed performance, Echo never got a hug again.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Thank you for welcoming me, Sally! I've practiced a few of my best pieces, I won't mess up the performance again!

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Great... I'm looking forward to it.
Sally nods with a smile and leads her inside before going off to attend to other things. Inside the auditorium, the charity concert is about to start and the audience is gradually taking their seats.
So, Echo finds an empty seat and sits down, thinking about Chief who was held up by an urgent task, and the conversation they had just before she left.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Echo, I promise, as soon as the mission is over, I'll rush to the concert.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Trust me, a promise is a promise. I'll definitely be there, as your most loyal spectator.
Hi, are you one of the performers today?
A sudden question from the side catches Echo off guard, and she notices that the spectators around her are eyeing her and the instrument in her hands.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Yes, that's right!

steps.speaker: Spectator A
steps.content: Your saxophone is quite unique. Seems like you cherish it a lot.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Yes, it's called Kute. It's my best friend and my best partner!

steps.speaker: Spectator A
steps.content: Haha, it even has a name?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Yes! It's been with me for a very long time. Even though it looks old, it can still make the most wonderful sounds!
The number of people chatting with Echo increases, and the girl can hardly contain her excitement. She feels that she made the right choice by coming here today!

steps.speaker: Spectator B
steps.content: The performance won't start for a while, could you give us a little preview?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Hmm... I'll save the pieces I prepared for later. For now, I'll improvise a little something for everyone!
Echo raises her saxophone with a serious look, closes her eyes, and starts playing with all her heart.
In her head, beautiful notes are constantly flowing out of the brass tube, spreading joy in the air, and all the listeners are intoxicated by it...
As the melody ends, a satisfied smile forms on Echo's lips as she slowly opens her eyes.
However, the faces around her aren't smiling like her, but rather showing a variety of strange expressions.

Some people are twitching at the corners of their eyes, some look pale, and some even cover their ears tightly. When they notice her gaze, they hurriedly lower their hands and awkwardly tug at the corners of their mouths.

steps.speaker: Spectator A
steps.content: Uh, not bad, that's some... unique music...

steps.speaker: Spectator B
steps.content: I need to go to the restroom, excuse me...
No applause nor praise, unlike what she expected. The audience who were just curious about her scatter like birds. Before Echo can react and think about it, Sally comes over and holds Echo's wrist.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: The performance is about to start, let's go backstage.
Her old friend, Sally, has a polite smile on her face. Echo can only nod, hold her saxophone tightly, and follow her.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Why hasn't Chief arrived yet...
While Echo is rehearsing the pieces she's going to play in her head, she keeps checking her terminal, but the person she is waiting for never sends a message.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Echo, you're up next, are you ready?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Sally, I think I might need to wait a bit longer...

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Why? I thought you were looking forward to getting on stage.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Because, I'm waiting for someone important...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Can I swap places with other performers? Just move my performance to a later slot.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: My spectator hasn't arrived yet, we agreed that I have to wait for him before I can start my performance...
steps.female_content: My spectator hasn't arrived yet, we agreed that I have to wait for her before I can start my performance...

steps.content: After hearing Echo's somewhat incoherent request, Sally shakes her head, looking slightly troubled.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: You're the last one, Echo.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: If you don't go on stage... I can only tell them the concert is over.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Ah... in that case...

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: It's your call. But if that person is really looking forward to your performance, and you give up now, wouldn't it be even more disappointing to him?
steps.female_content: It's your call. But if that person is really looking forward to your performance, and you give up now, wouldn't it be even more disappointing to her?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Hmm, You're right... Let's go then!
The curtain rises, the lights fall, and the young saxophonist is personally led to the center of the stage by the concert organizer.

steps.speaker: Spectator A
steps.content: Um... Isn't she the terrible saxophone player from earlier...
As soon as they see her, the audience who have heard Echo's playing before start to discuss among themselves.

steps.speaker: Spectator B
steps.content: She's really a performer? I thought she was just messing around.

steps.speaker: Spectator C
steps.content: Yeah, how come you guys really let her on stage? My kid cried after listening to her earlier!
They clamor, telling others how awful Echo's performance was, and loudly question Sally as to why she would invite such a poor musician for the final performance of the day.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Please, everyone, may I have your attention?
Sally calmly brings the microphone to her lips, soothing the audience with a smile.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Everyone is used to hearing beautiful and elegant music, but have you ever tried those fresh and intriguing tunes?

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: There's a rumor going around Eastside. A notorious homeless, known for their oddity, plays all sorts of discordant tunes on the streets. They say that noise is even more horrifying than the shrieks of a Corruptor...

steps.speaker: Spectator C
steps.content: I think I've heard this rumor before...

steps.speaker: Spectator D
steps.content: Is that true? Can someone really play such a ridiculous sound?

steps.speaker: Spectator C
steps.content: If that sounds anything like what she played... that might be true.

steps.speaker: Spectator D
steps.content: Interesting, I'd like to hear it!

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: So, to satisfy everyone's curiosity, I've invited a special guest today.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Yes, you've guessed it! The one on stage right now is the tone-deaf musician whose skills are worse than a third-rate artist's, yet more flamboyant and confident than a superstar. Let's give it up for the "fourth-rate artist," Echo!

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Now, please enjoy her saxophone solo performance!
The applause is thunderous, and the audience stops protesting. But Echo just stands there, looking lost...

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: What's the matter, Echo? Why aren't you starting? Everyone is waiting for you.
Seeing that Echo hasn't started playing, Sally steps forward and holds her in her arms, as gentle as when she first welcomed her.
Echo trembles in her arms, trying hard to maintain her usual cheerful tone, her voice shaking as she speaks.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Sally, stop joking around, this isn't funny at all...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Do you know? I've been preparing for today's concert for a long time!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Three other excellent musicians have been helping me rehearse... My performance tonight will be the most exciting one!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Also, do you remember when we used to live together in the orphanage? ...Back then you all praised my singing, clapped for me, and said that I would definitely become a superstar when I grew up...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Now I'm here to prove it to you, you were right, I...!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: ...What you said... tone-deaf, noise... You were just joking, right?

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: ...You're still so naive, Echo.
Sally sighs helplessly.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: It's time to wake up from your dream. You've grown up, but you haven't become a superstar, have you?

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: After all these years, you still seriously believe those lies we told you? I'm telling you the truth out of the goodness of my heart and you don't believe it. You're... such a fool.
Echo freezes, looking incredulously at the girl in front of her, trying to find any hint of a joke on her face.
But she fails. The face of her old friend, hidden in the shadows, is full of mockery. Sally leans into Echo's ear and whispers, each word she utters is heart-wrenching.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: You want to know the truth? Alright then... You were a joke when you were so engrossed in your playing even though you were completely out of tune. In the dull and boring orphanage, you were the only fun we had.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: In order to keep this "fun," we agreed to lie to you, just so you wouldn't discover the truth.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: But we didn't expect that you would have no self-awareness at all, and even made a fool of yourself at the most important annual party, turning everyone else into a joke!
Many years ago, an annual party at the Eastside Orphanage.
Ribbons, burst balloons, and instruments scatter all over the floor, the audience whispering in hushed voices.

steps.speaker: Adopter A
steps.content: Oh my goodness, she's so off-key... Does she have some kind of condition? Why didn't the institution take her to a check-up?

steps.speaker: Adopter B
steps.content: No way, are the children in this orphanage all like this...?

steps.speaker: Adopter C
steps.content: I can't take a child with a hidden illness home. Excuse me, I'm leaving.

steps.speaker: Sponsor
steps.content: This is how you planned your annual party, by having a tone-deaf kid on stage? This is a disaster!

steps.speaker: Dean
steps.content: We are truly sorry, we didn't know she would suddenly run up on stage, it was an oversight...

steps.speaker: Dean
steps.content: Echo! You little brat! Do you have any idea what you've done tonight?!

steps.speaker: Little Sally
steps.content: ...I heard from the volunteer teachers that the people who were ready to adopt have decided not to come. Many of the ongoing adoptions have also been terminated.

steps.speaker: Orphan A
steps.content: It's all Echo's fault! She insisted on going up to sing! She ruined everything!

steps.speaker: Orphan B
steps.content: Does she really think she sings well with that voice? It was so out-of-tune, how embarrassing!

steps.speaker: Orphan C
steps.content: Sob... I don't want to stay in the orphanage... Sob sob... I won't talk to her ever again...

steps.speaker: Orphan A
steps.content: Let's shut that annoying mouth from now on. Shut her up! That's what happens to bad guys! She deserves it!

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: You remember now? What a harsh world, right? I was also one of the children whose adoption was canceled back then.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Since then, no one has come to adopt me, and the orphanage has been quiet since, it's no different from an overgrown garden.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Ordinary music concerts can't attract the attention of the public these days, so I need a new gimmick to make everyone notice us, and that's you, Echo.
Sally says with a smirk, cruelly bursting the fragile bubble that has been wrapping Echo's beautiful dream.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: If you don't believe me, look at the audience. Whether they've heard you before or not, they're all expecting what horrible sounds you can make.
Echo stiffly looks around at the audience, where every pair of eyes is filled with curiosity and mockery.
This malicious attention, completely different from what she imagined, makes Echo shiver, as if she's back in that icy winter night. But this time, there's no miraculous melody to save her.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: You see now? Very good.

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: I'm glad you haven't improved at all. This is the opportunity for you to make amends. This is what you owe us.
When you hastily arrive at the concert venue, this is what you see.
Echo, with her head down, is in a young woman's embrace, clutching her saxophone as if it were her last lifeline.
Her face is flushed red, even the freckles on her nose are crinkled together, her eyes are brimming with tears, but she stubbornly refuses to let them fall.

Through the shackles, you sense that Echo is on the verge of a breakdown... She's shaken, questioning herself after persisting for years; she's in pain, because her fantasy has been shattered, and the harsh reality is right in her face.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm here, Echo!
You immediately jump onto the stage and grab Echo's hand. As you pull her away from Sally, you can feel she's trembling.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Chief, you're finally here...

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Tell me, is my playing really that bad?

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Am I really sick, like you said? Was all my effort just a joke in everyone's eyes?
Before you can answer, the audience starts to stir. All they see is a performer wasting their time and you who appear out of nowhere. The voices of dissatisfaction in the crowd grow louder.

steps.speaker: Audience
steps.content: What's going on, why hasn't the performance started yet!

steps.speaker: Sally
steps.content: Sir, you...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Please, give us a moment.
You raise your hand to stop her from approaching. Ignoring the surroundings, you cup Echo's face with your hands, making her focus on you. You tell her in your softest, most determined voice.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That's not true, Echo.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're not a joke, and your efforts aren't meaningless. After practicing and training all this time, you've proven your capabilities.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Echo, you've improved. Your playing has gotten much better, your music is not just terrible noises now. Even Dudu and the others are proud of your training results. So believe in yourself.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: But I'm tone deaf, I...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Tone-deafness is a symptom of amusia, but it's not your fault. Don't blame yourself for something you can't control.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Echo, think about why you have to come here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You said you want to return to this stage and make up for that performance with a perfect one.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: But I...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Remember everything Dudu and the others taught you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Those fingerings, techniques, breathing rhythms, and the saxophone playing method that I don't quite understand. Your memory is outstanding, as long as you can recall those muscle memories, you can do it.
Echo takes a deep breath, fuddling with the saxophone in her hand, her nervous expression slightly eased.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: ...You'll be watching me in the audience, right?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course, I promised you. When you play, I'll be watching and supporting you in the audience.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Even if everyone here thinks you're a joke, to me, you're always a promising saxophonist.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: ...Yes!
Echo smiles, nodding at you firmly. Her eyes are brimming with tears, but her heart no longer wavers. At this moment, she feels like she's been saved by another miracle.
The girl stands in the center of the stage, the spotlight shining on her, like a streetlight on a winter night.
She closes her eyes.
What is she thinking about? That near-death cold night, or her somewhat unique life now?
Or perhaps it's the orphanage life after she was forced to stop singing, or the carefree happiness from her nomadic days?
None of that matters now. You know that, to Echo, the most important thing is here and now, she plays her own, living tune with the saxophone.

steps.speaker: Saxophone
steps.content: Woooo!

The music ends. It's not a horrifically discordant tune as imagined, but a smooth, occasionally off-key rendition of a few classic pieces. The rowdy audience suddenly loses interest, applauding half-heartedly.

steps.speaker: Spectator D
steps.content: That's it? Just an average beginner, not terribly off-putting.

steps.speaker: Spectator C
steps.content: Well, it's much better than when she was playing before the concert...
Echo opens her eyes, not to look at the audience's reaction, but to search for you. The moment she finds you, she hugs her saxophone, jumps off the stage, and rushes towards you.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Chief, Chief! How was it?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Very good. To me, that was a perfect performance!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Really? I was actually very nervous just now...

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: It was really good. You've improved a lot, totally worth our long practice sessions. Well done!

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Dudu, Joan, Peggy... How come you're all here!
Echo looks at the three who suddenly appeared in disbelief, too stunned to speak.

steps.speaker: Peggy
steps.content: We couldn't stop worrying about you, so we came with Chief. We listened to the whole thing!

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: I'm quite satisfied with the performance, but this is the result of your own persistence and hard work.
As Joan speaks, she takes out a pick and places it in Echo's palm.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: You like collecting these things, right? Here, a new one for you. Let's keep playing together in the future. Your style might be unconventional, but if you find the right path, you can create unique music.

steps.speaker: Joan
steps.content: But it will be a difficult path. Now that you understand your own situation, give it some thought.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I-I... Of course, it would be an honor to play with you!
Unable to find any words to express her emotions, the tears Echo's been holding back finally fall.
After the concert, you return to the Bureau with your Sinners.
Although it was quite eventful, fortunately, things turned out alright. On your way back, Echo has agreed to the treatment for amusia.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Chief, do you know? Before you showed up, I was about to give up.
You listen quietly, not interrupting her heartfelt confession.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: The moment I found out the truth, I realized that I'm not some genius musician. I can't play perfect music with the saxophone. It was all my wishful thinking.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: And those imaginations... were once my motivation to keep on living.
Echo takes a deep breath, trying hard to hold back her tears.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I should have given up when my fantasy was shattered, but I heard your voice.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: With such a warm voice, you told me that there's always a turning point, that I can still continue my performance on stage. You gave me courage and strength.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: So I think... perhaps I can turn fantasy into a dream with hard work... If I could play a normal tune by practicing, I might be able to achieve my goal.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: I'm still a little scared... but I've decided to try to accept my flaw. I want to tell people with my music that, just like me, everyone can be saved in times of despair and helplessness.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: The saxophone saved me last time, this time it was you. Thank you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Choice
options: It wasn't just your saxophone, or me.

choices.text: It wasn't just your saxophone, or me.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You saved yourself too. Everything you've been through, the path you've taken... these have all become the strength to keep you going.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Those who can bravely face reality and choose to start over can certainly play more powerful music.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm still waiting for your exclusive concert, the most-promising saxophonist.
Echo laughs heartily, this time, the corners of her eyes are adorned with tears of gratitude.

steps.speaker: Echo
steps.content: Someday, my most loyal spectator!
Under the streetlights on a winter night, a homeless girl picks up a worn saxophone at the entrance of the theatre, carefully cradling it in her arms.
This night will be free of sorrow, and this winter will not be long and harsh.
